description: Read a file from the filesystem. Returns up to 2000 lines starting at an optional offset. For files over 32 KiB, reading without an explicit line range returns a SYMBOL OUTLINE (function / class / heading names with line numbers) â€” or, if the file has no code structure, its first 1 KiB â€” instead of the full content; use start_line + end_line (or offset + limit) on a follow-up read to fetch the specific section you want. description: Modify an EXISTING file by applying one or more targeted text substitutions. PREFER this tool over `write` whenever you are changing only part of a file â€” it streams less data and produces a reviewable diff. Pass `edits: [{old_text, new_text}, ...]`; every edit is applied in order. `old_text` is matched FUZZILY using line-level edit-distance â€” minor whitespace, indentation, smart-quote / dash, and single-character typo drift between the snippet you saw and the file on disk are tolerated automatically. Match the snippet as faithfully as you can; if `old_text` could plausibly refer to more than one region of the file, add surrounding context to disambiguate, OR pass `line: N` (1-based) to anchor the match near a known line. To replace multiple occurrences pass either `replace_all: true` (replace every hit) or `expected_replacements: N` (replace exactly N hits, fail if the count differs â€” safer for refactors). No-op edits (old_text == new_text) are silently skipped, not errors. Include a brief `display_description` (e.g. 'Fix null-deref in auth.cpp') â€” it shows in the card while edits stream.

display_description.description: One-line summary shown in the card while edits stream â€” e.g. 'Fix null-deref in auth.cpp'. Stream second.

edits.description: One or more edits, applied in order.

expected_replacements.description: If set, edit must match exactly this many times or it fails. Safer than replace_all for known-count refactors â€” surfaces mismatches as errors instead of silent over-replace.

line.description: 1-based line number anchor for ambiguous matches. If old_text could match multiple regions, the one closest to this line (within ~200 lines) wins. Optional.

new_text.description: Replacement text. Indentation is auto-adjusted to match the surrounding file convention when old_text was at a different indent level.

old_text.description: Snippet to find. Matched fuzzily by line edit-distance â€” minor whitespace/indent drift and single-char typos are tolerated. Should be unique in the file OR accompanied by `line` to disambiguate.

Do NOT use POSIX-only commands (`uname`, `cat /etc/os-release`, `sw_vers`, `ls`, `grep`, `sed`, `awk`, heredocs) â€” they will fail. Do NOT use for file IO â€” use the write/edit/read tools instead.
